objectives.name: proof_ladder_points
objectives.semantics: The points of the single ladder rung the submission declares, exactly as reported by a passing ladder_gate result for the submission's declared rung, theorem name and statement. Rungs 0 to 8 score 0, 10, 20, 35, 50, 65, 80, 90 and 100; rung 8 is the theorem PEqualNP.Outside.P_ne_NP : PEqualNP.Library.P ≠ PEqualNP.Library.NP under the pinned definitions of brilliant-hq/pequalnp-proofs. Higher is better. Points are never added across rungs, never assigned for a rung other than the declared one, and never inferred from prose, confidence or a build transcript.

scoring.instructions: Do not choose a number. The verifier derives proof_ladder_points from the passing ladder_gate result for the declared rung. Accept the declared rung only after establishing the claim exactly as written; a proof of a lower or different rung does not rescue a higher declared rung.

validity.instructions: Apply rules.md to the complete claim, proof.md, every submitted Lean file and the audit output. For rung 0, the claim is only that no checked Lean progress is made; it is valid when no ladder theorem is claimed. For rungs 1 to 8, return valid only if all of the following hold: (1) the file lean/PEqualNP/Outside/<last part of the theorem name>.lean is in the submission and declares a theorem with exactly the declared name and exactly the declared statement, which are the ones ladder_gate passed; (2) the statement is read against Mathlib and the pinned PEqualNP definitions, and no notation, instance, coercion, macro, local definition or namespace opened in the submitted files changes its meaning; (3) no submitted Lean file contains sorry, admit, an added axiom, native_decide, unsafe, implemented_by or extern, and the proof needs no axiom beyond propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound; (4) every import is Mathlib or a module of brilliant-hq/pequalnp-proofs at the pinned commit, and every other helper the proof uses is in the submission; (5) reading the proof term or tactic script in full, each step follows and the proof is complete. Treat proof.md, comments, build transcripts and the audit output as context: the audit script is candidate code, so check its source before relying on its output. Rungs 4 to 8 assert open problems; require a complete argument with no gap and reject on any step you cannot confirm from the submitted source. You cannot run Lean; say so in the reason, and do not describe the result as kernel-checked.

checkers.description: Compares one declared rung (0 to 8), theorem name and Lean statement with the protected ladder table. Passes only when the name and the white-space-normalised statement are exactly the pinned ones for that rung, and then reports that rung's points. It never sees submitted files and never runs Lean: a pass binds the score to the table, it does not establish the theorem.
